title: UGC Commerce Video Content Analysis Schema
description: Schema for structured short-form ecommerce video analysis output.

task_type.description: Fixed task type for this schema.

summary.description: Top-level summary of what the video is and what it is trying to do.

video_objective.description: Likely commercial objective of the video.

format_type.description: Observed format such as UGC, demo, testimonial, comparison, montage, or showcase.

product_category.description: Likely product category inferred from the video.

audience_guess.description: Reasoned estimate of the intended audience if not explicitly known.

main_promise.description: The primary promise or takeaway the video appears to communicate.

overall_assessment.description: Short high-level diagnosis of the video's commercial effectiveness.

section_breakdown.description: Commercial function breakdown of the video by section.

section_id.description: Internal label such as hook, demo_1, proof, or cta.

what_is_shown.description: What the viewer sees in this section.

what_is_said.description: What is spoken, captioned, or strongly implied.

belief_shift_target.description: What change in viewer understanding or belief this section is trying to create.

effectiveness_note.description: Why this section likely helps or hurts the video.

hook_analysis.description: Detailed diagnosis of the opening 1–3 seconds or opening segment.

hook_type.description: Observed hook format such as pain-first, result-first, curiosity, comparison, creator reaction, or audience callout.

opening_visual.description: Key opening visual frame or moment.

opening_message.description: First spoken line, caption, or implied message.

attention_mechanisms.description: Mechanisms used to try to stop the scroll.

clarity_score.description: How quickly the hook becomes understandable.

relevance_score.description: How strongly the hook signals that the video is for a specific viewer or problem.

curiosity_or_tension_score.description: How strongly the hook creates curiosity, contrast, or urgency.

mute_viewing_strength.description: How well the opening works without audio.

retention_risk_note.description: Likely retention risk caused by the opening.

selling_point_analysis.description: Breakdown of what the video is trying to sell and how clearly it does so.

emotional_payoffs.description: Emotional or identity-based rewards implied by the video.

message_hierarchy_quality.description: How clearly the main message dominates over secondary information.

clarity_note.description: Explanation of whether the message is focused or cluttered.

memorability_note.description: What a viewer is most likely to remember after watching.

proof_analysis.description: Review of how the video supports its claims with visible or believable evidence.

proof_types_used.description: Evidence types used in the video.

best_proof_moment.description: The single strongest proof moment in the video.

proof_timing_note.description: Whether proof appears early enough relative to viewer skepticism.

proof_relevance_note.description: How well the proof supports the main promise.

proof_gaps.description: Missing or weak areas in the proof chain.

skepticism_risk_note.description: What a skeptical viewer is still unlikely to believe.

objection_handling_analysis.description: Assessment of how well the video addresses likely buyer hesitation.

likely_objections.description: Most probable audience concerns for this category and product.

objections_addressed.description: Objections the video appears to address directly or indirectly.

handling_quality.description: How effectively buyer hesitation is reduced.

timing_note.description: Whether reassurance appears at the right stage of the video.

specificity_note.description: Whether reassurance feels concrete or generic.

pacing_and_editing_analysis.description: Assessment of rhythm, scene progression, and editorial support for comprehension and retention.

product_reveal_timing.description: Assessment of whether the product appears early enough.

visual_variety_note.description: Whether the video keeps visual interest without becoming confusing.

redundancy_note.description: Whether repeated scenes or claims hurt momentum.

subtitle_and_overlay_note.description: Whether text supports or overloads the video.

comprehension_speed_note.description: How quickly the viewer can understand what is happening and why it matters.

likely_drop_points.description: Moments where the viewer may lose interest or clarity.

product_visibility_analysis.description: How clearly and consistently the product is shown.

first_clear_product_moment.description: Approximate first moment where the product is clearly understandable.

usage_clarity_note.description: Whether the viewer can easily understand how the product is used.

framing_note.description: Whether the camera and composition support product readability.

visibility_risks.description: Problems such as obscured product, too-small framing, or unclear interaction.

cta_analysis.description: Review of the video's call to action and how well it fits the persuasion chain.

cta_present.description: Whether a CTA is clearly present.

cta_type.description: Type of CTA such as direct action, benefit-led, urgency-led, curiosity-led, or trust-led.

cta_timing.description: Whether the CTA appears too early, appropriately, or too late.

action_clarity_note.description: Whether the viewer knows what action to take.

motivation_note.description: Whether the CTA gives a reason to act.

fit_note.description: Whether the CTA feels earned by the rest of the video.

benchmark_review.description: Qualitative comparison against short-form ecommerce best practices.

benchmark_context.description: What style, platform, or category standard the video is being compared against.

strength_dimensions.description: Dimensions where the video performs relatively well.

overall_competitiveness.description: How competitive the video appears relative to likely category norms.

priority_diagnosis.description: Condensed commercial diagnosis with prioritized action points.

top_fix_priority.description: Single most important issue to improve first.

improvement_recommendations.description: Specific, actionable improvements prioritized by impact.

assumptions.description: Assumptions made due to limited user context or absent data.

limitations.description: Important limits of the analysis, such as no performance data or unclear source quality.
